content.text: {"label":"outage","confidence":"high","explanation":"Calls to the general queue jumped from about 64 per interval to 114–124 from 14:30, roughly 70–97% above forecast, and service level fell as low as 12.2%. Most of the extra calls are login_issue: 237 against 59.2 expected (4.0x normal, 177.8 of about 221 excess calls). This lines up with P2 incident INC-20261015-6270, opened at 14:50, where net banking and app login has been failing with HTTP 503 errors since a certificate rotation. The calls started rising at 14:15–14:30, just before the ticket was opened. The payments shortfall (32 agents vs 38 planned) is not a sick wave, since absences are normal at 2 vs 2.4 usual, and general has 6 more agents on the phones than planned (40 vs 34), so payments agents were probably moved to cover the outage.","evidence":[{"source":"incident","ref_id":"INC-20261015-6270","summary":"P2, opened 14:50: customers can't log in to net banking or the mobile app; the login service is returning HTTP 503 after a certificate rotation."},{"source":"reason_codes","ref_id":"login_issue","summary":"General, 14:00–15:15: 237 calls vs 59.2 expected (4.0x), share up from 15% to 38.5%; most of the excess calls."},{"source":"metrics","ref_id":"volume","summary":"General: 124, 115, 114 and 114 calls per interval from 14:30 vs about 63–67 forecast (+70% to +97%)."},{"source":"metrics","ref_id":"service_level","summary":"General service level fell to 16.9% and 12.2% at 14:30–14:45, then 33.3% at 15:15; 39 calls abandoned at 14:30."},{"source":"metrics","ref_id":"staffing","summary":"Payments has 32 agents on the phones vs 38 planned while general has 40 vs 34 planned, which points to agents moved between queues, not lost."},{"source":"attendance","ref_id":"attendance_log","summary":"Normal absence on both queues: payments 2 sick (usual 2.4), general 2 sick (usual 2.2).
